AN ACT to amend the election law, in relation to requiring the county seat in
Seneca county to have at least one polling place designated for early voting
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4944        Revised 2/19/2021

SPONSOR: HELMING
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the election law, in relation to requiring the county
seat in Seneca county to have at least one polling place designated for
early voting

 
PURPOSE:

Requires the county seat in Seneca County to have at least one polling
place designated for early voting.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one of this bill amends paragraph (a) of subdivision 2 of
section 8-600 of the Election Law to provide that the county seat of
Seneca County may be a designated as an early polling site for the
purposes of such law. (Amends Chapter 344 of 2020).

Section two is the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Chapter 344 of the laws of 2020 requires each county board of elections
to include at least one early voting site in the municipality with the
highest population in such county based on the latest federal decennial
census. Chapter 344 also provides that, to the extent practicable, if
such municipality has public transportation routes, such polling place
shall be situated along such transportation routes.

In the case of Seneca County, the Town of Seneca Falls, which is the
largest municipality in Seneca County, is located in close proximity to
the county seat, Waterloo. The Seneca County seat, Waterloo, is also
served by public transportation routes. Additionally, having this poll-
ing site located in the Seneca County Office Building along with the
Board of Elections is both beneficial for voters and instrumental in the
efficient use of time, money and resources. Thus, under these special
circumstances, it is appropriate to authorize Seneca County to designate
the county seat, Waterloo, as an early voting site in compliance with
Chapter 344.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill. (Similar bill has passed the Senate in 2021 - S.1310)

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

No fiscal implication to the State.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
By its terms, this act will be considered to have taken effect on Janu-
ary 1, 2021.
